balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Automatic Data Processing, Inc.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Automatic Data Processing, Inc.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Automatic Data Processing, Inc.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Automatic Data Processing, Inc.: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Automatic Data Processing, Inc.: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Automatic Data Processing, Inc.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Automatic Data Processing, Inc.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Automatic Data Processing, Inc.: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

segmentRevenue.title: Segment revenue: Employer Services vs PEO
segmentRevenue.content:
ADP reports two segments: Employer Services (payroll, HR, tax filing, sold directly) and PEO (co-employment, where ADP becomes the employer of record for client worksite employees).

For Automatic Data Processing, Inc.: PEO revenue includes pass-through benefits and payroll-tax costs, so it looks larger relative to Employer Services than the earnings split below suggests.

What to watch:

  • Employer Services growth, which carries ADP's software/platform margin
  • PEO revenue growth driven by worksite employee count vs. pass-through cost inflation

segmentEarnings.title: Segment earnings: Employer Services vs PEO
segmentEarnings.content:
Segment earnings (before corporate allocations) by business line. Employer Services carries most of ADP's margin; PEO earns a much thinner spread because its revenue includes pass-through costs it doesn't mark up.

For Automatic Data Processing, Inc.: compare this split against the revenue split above -- PEO's share of earnings is consistently smaller than its share of revenue.

What to watch:

  • Employer Services margin trend (new-business pricing, retention)
  • PEO earnings growth vs. worksite employee growth

peoPassThrough.title: PEO revenue vs pass-through costs
peoPassThrough.content:
In the PEO model, ADP bills clients for worksite employees' wages, benefits premiums and payroll taxes, then remits those amounts -- this pass-through portion is revenue by accounting convention but not ADP's own economics.

For Automatic Data Processing, Inc.: pass-through costs are typically the larger share of PEO segment revenue; ADP's actual take is closer to the gap between PEO revenue and this line, which is why PEO earnings (above) run far below its revenue share.

What to watch:

  • Pass-through costs rising faster than PEO revenue (benefits/payroll-tax inflation, not client growth)
  • Worksite employee growth as the real demand signal, not revenue alone

clientFunds.title: Client funds interest and yield
clientFunds.content:
ADP holds client payroll funds briefly between collection and payment to employees/tax authorities, and invests that float. Interest on funds held for clients is the income earned; yield is that income divided by the average balance invested.

For Automatic Data Processing, Inc.: this is a material, largely rate-driven income stream layered on top of the core payroll/HR business -- it rose sharply as short rates rose and will fall back as they ease, independent of client growth.

What to watch:

  • Yield tracking short-term rates, not ADP's own performance
  • Interest income as a share of pre-tax income, so a rate cycle isn't mistaken for operating momentum

clientGrowth.title: Pays per control and worksite employee growth
clientGrowth.content:
Pays per control is the y/y change in paychecks processed for the same client base (Employer Services) -- ADP's cleanest read on employment at existing clients. Worksite employee growth is the PEO equivalent.

For Automatic Data Processing, Inc.: both are same-client organic measures, stripped of new bookings and pricing -- a macro employment signal as much as a company one.

What to watch:

  • Negative or decelerating pays per control as a recession signal for ADP's own clients
  • Divergence between the two lines (Employer Services vs PEO client bases)

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Automatic Data Processing, Inc.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
